Monday, November 16, 2020  7:00 PM  Teleconference

Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Park and Activities Commission Members will be
participating via teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for viewing.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
827 9177 1252 , Meeting Password: 070197. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in
option from a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to Cynthia Morquecho, Community Services Supervisor at
cynthiam@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded
to the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 827 9177 1252, Meeting Password: 070197.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The Meeting Host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

AGENDA
  JANUARY 19, 2021
  ITEM NO.5A

  MINUTES

  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  NOVEMBER 16, 2020

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, and Romanelli

  Commissioners Absent: Retz

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Michael Goldsmith
  Comm. Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 19, 2020

  CHAIR PERSICHINA requested a revision to the bottom of page five of the first
  sentence.

  COMMISSIONER  ROMANELLI  made  a  motion,  seconded  by  CHAIR
  PERSICHINA to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 19, 2020 AS MODIFIED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  2021 COMMITTEE AND SUBCOMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview per the agenda
  material.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
   All assignments have remained the same.

  Assignments are as follows:

  2021 Standing Committee Representatives

  Equestrian Committee (Monthly as needed)............................................... Ciarolla
  Traffic and Safety Committee (Quarterly as needed) .................................... Romanelli
  Environmental Advisory Committee (Quarterly as needed) ............................. Bain

  2021 Commission Subcommittee Members

  Tracy Austin Doubles Tennis Tournament Subcommittee… ............. Romanelli, Pope, McCormick
  The Hills Are Alive Race Subcommittee .........................................Persichina, Ciarolla, Romanelli
  City Celebration Subcommittee ............................................................................ Retz & Ciarolla
  Peninsula Holiday Parade of Lights Subcommittee............................... Persichina, Pope, McCormick
  Youth Sports Subcommittee ................................................................... Bain, Persichina, Romanelli

  2021 Adopt-A-Park Assignments

  Ernie Howlett Park ............................................................................ Persichina
  Highridge Park ................................................................................. Bain
  Rockbluff Park ................................................................................. Romanelli
  Chandler & Pepperwood Parks ............................................................. Ciarolla
  Silver Spur Park ............................................................................... Pope
  Dapplegray & Butcher Parks ................................................................ Retz
  George F Canyon Nature Center, Preserve & Taber Grove… ......................... McCormick

  B.  HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated that staff is recruiting partners for
  displays. Silver Spur Little League and Lomita Sheriff have confirmed their participation.
  The presenting sponsor is Cal Water and Waste Management has confirmed sponsorship
  as well. Sheriff are working with staff for a traffic plan for the event. Advertisement on
  Facebook has reached over 21,000 people. The event has been shared 40 times and 190
  people have been registered for the event to gauge attendance. Local cities and officials
  have been contacted to attend the event. Staff is looking for volunteers to help paint the
  displays as well.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked staff if the Chamber of Commerce has been
  contacted to reach out to the businesses on the Peninsula. Community Services
  Supervisor Morquecho responded they have been contacted.

  C.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE RECOGNITION PLAQUE REQUEST

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief review of the staff report.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
   VICE CHAIR POPE moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK, TO
  APPROVE STAFF RECOMMENDATION AS FOLLOWS:

  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION APPROVAL OF THE EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE’S REQUEST TO INSTALL INDIVIDUAL DEDICATION PLAQUES
  FOR RETIRED TRAINER JAN BALL AT PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER
  AND ROLLING HILLS ESTATES RESIDENT CAROL DEAN PORTER AT THE
  JUDGE’S BOOTH OF ERNIE HOWLETT PARK AND PROVIDE DIRECTION ON
  THE PURPOSED RECOGNITION WALL.

  AYES:  Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Romanelli
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Retz, Bain

  The motion carries.

  D.  TABER GROVE UPDATE

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a brief overview of the staff report.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if multiple bids will be received for the project. Assistant
  City manager Davis noted that since it is a Public Works project at least three bids
  will be sourced.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked about the funds and remaining balance.
  Assistant City Manager Davis responded that $44,000 is remaining for the project
  which will go to grading, trails, wood chips and erosion control. The $40,000
  expenditure was due to Wildan Engineering cost. The $100,000 donation will not be
  exceeded.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR POPE, TO APPROVE
  STAFF RECOMMENDATION AS FOLLOWS:

  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION RECOMMEND CITY COUNCIL
  AUTHORIZE STAFF TO PROCEED WITH BIDDING THE PROJECT.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  7.  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION

  A.  PEPPER TREE BYLAWS REVIEW

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a brief review of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN entered the meeting at 7:33 P.M.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
   COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if the number of requests to the Foundation will be affected
  by the review and the capacity of the Foundation to address the requests and if staff has
  a sense of the additional deliberation that would occur from the increased requests.
  Assistant City Manager Davis responded that the examples provided would be done
  regardless of the Pepper Tree Foundation explaining that a lot of the programs could fall
  into the expanded purposes of the Foundation. COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the broad
  purposes of the proposed bylaws that the Commission may not have competence to
  review and is concerned that the Commission may be distracted by looking at proposals
  that may not represent the heart of the City.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if there was a need to move forward with the revised bylaws
  tonight. Assistant City Manager Davis responded that the proposal is not under any rush
  and can be looked at in the January meeting.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted his concern is the dilution of the original intent of
  the Pepper Tree Foundation from a financial checks and balances standpoint. He noted if
  a person were to donate funds to go towards parks and trails, they may be spent on the
  other items included in the Pepper Tree Foundations revised bylaws. He suggests that the
  Pepper Tree Foundation structure subaccounts to direct funds to the desired areas within
  the Foundation.

  VICE CHAIR POPE explained that the term “activities” in the Parks and Activities
  commission is fairly broad supporting the expanded scope. She agrees with the flexibility
  of the revised bylaws and that they should be reviewed and updated and explained that
  there are ways to honor donor intent without putting restrictions on giving. VICE CHAIR
  POPE stated that expansion of the bylaws will allow to meet the City’s needs as they arrive
  and also give the donor the ability to choose how their donations are spent.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted donors may restrict their donations which may not provide
  for operating expenses and over-head that non-profits have. She agrees with VICE CHAIR
  POPE and added that restrictions to receiving donations may hinder the operation of the
  Foundation which may be problematic for the Commission to mediate. She also noted that
  the “activities” in Parks and Activities were limited to activities within the parks that would
  benefit the parks and trails. COMMISSIONER BAIN explained that the categories seem
  unclear as to how they would relate to the City and if they are restricted to the parks.
  COMMISSIONER ROMENALLI explained that he did not intend to add restrictions to
  receiving funds but that the funds would be applied to what the donors suggested; and
  clearly be directed to those areas.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted there is some control on donations and that funds
  do not have to be taken if there are restrictions. He furthered that the proposed expanded
  categories seem to have already been in place as is evident from past events.

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho added such projects like the Veteran’s
  Memorial will draw a clear line as to how the money is donated and spent within the
  Foundation but is still brought to the Commission for approval.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
   COMMISSIONER BAIN noted if a donation is given for a single purpose then it would only
  be spent on that purpose but that monies accumulated up until the point of the revised
  bylaws would be up for grabs for the Foundation.

  Assistant City Manager Davis stated individual gifts are typically focused in scope and
  analyzed closely by staff and approved by City Council, such as the Taber Grove donation,
  with event sponsor dollars typically deposited in the Pepper Tree Foundation.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if donations from event sponsors were to have any
  strings attached to them. Assistant City Manager Davis responded that donations to a
  specific event would likely go toward that event or support the Foundation in general and
  annual reports from staff note such donations and are tracked accordingly. Assistant City
  Manager Davis explained that the Pepper Tree Foundation budget is annually reviewed
  and approved by the City Council as Board of Directors.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted his concern for funds going to the right place and
  is agrees with proceeding with the proposed expanded scope. COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK agrees.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if there were any expectation on how the Foundation would
  be run with the expanded scope because the Commission may not have the bandwidth to
  consider the subjects considered. Assistant City Manager Davis noted staff would go to
  the Commission for approval for new programs as has been done in the past. She
  furthered that at the moment, the only expansion to the Committee would be the
  fundraising committee; however there is no current recommendation for additional
  committees, nor any present inconsistencies to what the Commission is currently
  handling.

  VICE CHAIR POPE moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK, TO ACCEPT
  STAFF RECOMMENDATION AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  THE PEPPER TREE ADVISORY BOARD REVIEW, PROVIDE INPUT AND
  RECOMMEND THE FINAL DRAFT OF THE UPDATED PEPPER TREE
  FOUNDATION BYLAWS TO BE REVIEWED AND APPROVED BY THE PEPPER
  TREE FOUNDATION BOARD OF DIRECTORS.

  AYES:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Romanelli
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Retz

  The motion carries.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted Highridge Park’s parking lot was full and trash was mostly
  under control with one trash can that seemed broken. She additionally reported dog
  walkers seem to put dog waste in the recycling bin; all exercise equipment has been

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
   removed; bathrooms were clean; and pooling of water is under control. She explained that
  now with playgrounds open, she observed heavy use with about 50% of adults present
  without masks or social distancing.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted a bite mark on the fence at Dapplegray Park.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted the upgraded footing in the area and that
  the bite mark is rot but will be taken care of shortly.

  9.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Assistant City Manager Davis noted increased case numbers in the County. The state has
  issued a travel advisory and cities outside of Los Angeles County are moving back in
  restricted tiers. The County Health Department is encouraging staying at home and limiting
  Holiday gatherings over the next few weeks. Recreation activities have not seen any
  required limitations as of yet.

  B.  SPECIAL EVENTS AND RECREATION PROGRAMS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted the Veteran’s Memorial Ceremony was
  dedicated on Tuesday November 10th. Donor, Mr. Chidsey was very happy with the garden
  and plaques and wanted to congratulate the Commission for making it happen. The
  Mayor’s Ride was opened on Saturday November 14th, riders will be given a key chain and
  horse treats when visiting Kelly’s Korner at the end of the tour. The December movie night
  will take place on the 17th and will show “Elf”. The event was sold out within two hours and
  was limited to Peninsula residents.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested seeing if there was a way to manage a wait list for
  those wanting to see the film.

  Assistant City Manager Davis asked if the spots provided were over-capacity. Community
  Services Supervisor Morquecho responded that it was offered over capacity with 80 spots
  available. The last event in October offered 60 spots with only 30 cars participated, which
  was why the spots were increased for December. The difficulty is whether or not
  reservations will arrive the day of the event. COMMISSSIONER BAIN suggested having
  attendees arrive earlier to manage spots or have spots released if not filled in time or
  charging for the event.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the Parade budget was satisfactory. Community
  Services Supervisor Morquecho stated the majority of the budget goes towards the lighting
  company and that community partners are relied upon for display locations.

  VICE CHAIR POPE noted the success of the October Movie Nigh and stated that charging
  a nominal fee may ensure greater attendance in the future. COMMISSIONER BAIN added
  a raffle could be implemented to ensure attendance as well.

  C.  COMMISSION MEETING DECEMBER 21, 2020 (VERBAL REPORT)

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
   Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted the December meeting is typically
  cancelled due to holiday and asked if the Commission would like to meet in December or
  reschedule to the January meeting. CHAIR PERSICHINA will not be available and votes
  on skipping the meeting. VICE CHAIR POPE asked if there would be any pressing
  agendas for the December meeting, if not, the meeting can be skipped. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI asked if the meeting could be cancelled a week before it begins. Community
  Services Supervisor Morquecho responded that staff will contact the Commission by email
  around that time for confirmation. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the agenda
  could be sent with the email so that the Commissioners can review for any pressing items.
  Assistant City Manager Davis stated December is typically a light meeting in case there is
  a cancellation; new Committee assignments would be the biggest item which has been
  approved at this meeting.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF OCTOBER 27, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  E-BIKE BUSINESS

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated staff is still waiting on the business
  owner on whether their business plan is being accepted by other nearby cities.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the proposed parking area was quite full on Sunday
  and that a limited amount of space be suggested for the business.

  B.  PICKLEBALL

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated staff is currently working on
  receiving quotes for permanent lines and the feasibility of temporary lines.

  C.  HIGHRIDGE PARK MURAL

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho stated staff is still working with the artist
  on updated drafts for the mural.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated he would like to coordinate the annual holiday
  lunch for the maintenance crew with Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith.
  Commissioners will donate to the lunch.

  Assistant City Manager Davis noted that Council member Judy Mitchell will be retiring
  from the City Council after 20 years of service with her final meeting on December 8th.
  Farewell videos are encouraged to be sent to staff to show at the following Council
  meeting.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
   12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 8:31 PM TO AN ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON JANUARY 21, 2020 AT 7:00 P.M. IN THE CITY
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4045 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Daniel A-Haja  Cynthia Morquecho
  Community Services Coordinator  Community Services Supervisor

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
NOVEMBER 16, 2020
